title: Ring of Fire Air operator policy A (default)
label: ILLUSTRATIVE, not an airline SRA
summary_text: Operator policy A (default, illustrative): the current VAA and SIGMET affected areas, merged, up to the highest top, are treated as high contamination and avoided at dispatch. This follows the Doc 9974 App 5 5.4(d)(2) default for ungraded areas, "unless the operator’s safety risk assessment allows it to do otherwise safely". Where a State grades contamination (Doc 9974 App 5 5.4(d)(1)), Policy A still treats every graded area as high contamination. Under Doc 9974 2.10 an operator whose SMS shows it can do so safely may plan through, under or over (Policy B). In this build an airborne level change can still place a flight above or below the area with the vertical margin; such an advisory carries an OVER ASH or UNDER ASH line saying Policy A advises avoiding the area, and no drift-down or escape check is made.

vertical_margin_ft.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: added above the hazard top and below its base. For comparison, UK practice puts the assumed minimum safe altitude at least 2,000 ft above the ash top (CAP 1236 2.24), does not permit operators without an appropriate SRA to fly beneath an area (CAP 1236 2.28), and for operators with one sets the maximum usable level beneath a moderate or high contamination area 2,000 ft below its base (CAP 1236 2.29).

search_radius_nm.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: alternates are looked for within this distance because the aircraft's endurance is unknown.

min_runway_m.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: a simplified jet-alternate rule on the longest runway length only (dry), not an airline's alternate approval.

min_visibility_m.source: TEPHRA illustrative planning minimum for the TAF screen, not an airline's alternate minima.

min_ceiling_ft.source: TEPHRA illustrative planning minimum for the TAF screen, not an airline's alternate minima.

taf_eta_window_min.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: TAF groups this many minutes either side of the ETA are screened.

terminal_radius_nm.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: an alternate is rejected when a disc of this radius around it touches the hazard area.

level_search_ft.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: a level change is proposed only when a clear band lies this close to the present level.

level_band_fl.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: the width of a proposed level band.

max_change_level_fl.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: the highest level TEPHRA proposes; above it many fleet types cannot go.

divert_within_min.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: with no clear band, entry this close makes the rules divert to an acceptable alternate.

hold_within_min.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: with no clear band and no diversion, entry this close makes the rules advise a hold. The same time applies when no official product is valid.

buffer_nm.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: lateral buffer kept outside the hazard area. No ICAO or UK figure exists (research/18a section 2); it must exceed the turn anticipation of a 90 degree turn at cruise speed (about 6.4 NM at 450 kt and 25 degrees of bank).

simplify_nm.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: Douglas-Peucker tolerance on the hazard outline; it is added to the buffer, so the simplified obstacle still contains the true area.

max_waypoints_count.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: at most this many inserted turn points. Four ICAO coordinates still fit one ACARS message and a dispatcher can check them; with three, a third of the flights in the jagged-hazard benchmark found no route (research/18a; NASA DWR inserts at most two around convective cells).

max_turn_deg.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: the largest track change allowed at a turn point.

rejoin_step_nm.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: spacing of the candidate points where the route rejoins the present track beyond the hazard.

max_extra_min.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: a lateral route longer than this many extra minutes is not offered; the planner weighs a level change, hold or diversion instead.

min_extra_min.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: a reroute saving less than this over the present track is reported as no benefit.

route_max_cross_track_nm.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: a published route is used only when the aircraft lies within this distance of that leg's great circle (VRS standing data is crowd-sourced).

cruise_tas_kt.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: true airspeed assumed for timing a route when ADS-B gives no ground speed (jet cruise).

min_turn_min.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: minimum ground time between two flights of one aircraft (narrowbody).

max_delay_min.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: a flight delayed longer than this is cancelled instead.

freeze_window_min.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: flights departing within this many minutes, and airborne flights, are not moved by the recovery model.

horizon_after_closure_min.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: the recovery model re-plans flights departing up to this long after the closure is expected to end.

scenario_extend_1_min.source: Closures were extended repeatedly in the 5-7 Sep 2026 Java event (CGK 05:30, then 09:30, then 18:00), so the recovery agent also plans for the closure lasting this much longer (research/18d section 7.1).

solve_work_s.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: CP-SAT deterministic time per scenario (about seconds of single-core work). A deterministic limit with interleaved search gives the same plan on every run; on the Krakatau replay it takes about 15 s on 8 cores and costs 767k USD, against 0.89-0.95M and a different plan each run with a 2 s wall-clock limit.

solve_time_limit_s.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: wall-clock guard per scenario; the deterministic limit normally ends the search first.

delay_cost_per_min_usd.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: placeholder fixed cost of one minute of delay (research/18d section 7.3).

delay_cost_per_pax_hour_usd.source: Placeholder delay cost per passenger-hour: 0.4 USD per minute x 0.85 load, about 20 USD (research/18d section 7.3).

cancel_cost_per_pax_usd.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: placeholder cost per booked passenger of a cancellation (research/18d section 7.3).

cancel_cost_fixed_usd.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: placeholder fixed cost of a cancellation (research/18d section 7.3).

swap_cost_usd.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: placeholder cost of moving a flight to another aircraft (research/18d section 7.3).

ferry_cost_per_block_min_usd.source: Placeholder ferry cost per block minute, near the A4A 2024 figure of 100.76 USD (research/18d section 7.3).

max_fdp_min.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: 13 h planning limit on a crew's flight duty period, inside the 14 h of CASR 121 (research/18d section 7.3).

airport_closure_radius_nm.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: an airport counts as closed while the hazard area at any level below FL100 comes within this distance, or its TAF or METAR reports VA.

pax_notice_min_delay_min.source: Indonesia PM 89/2015 Pasal 3: delay category 1 starts at 30 minutes (research/18d section 4.1); a delay shorter than this gets no passenger notice, a cancellation always does.

hold_min.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: the length of hold the fuel formula costs.

divert_extra_min.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: minutes added to a diversion's cruise time for the approach and landing.

unexposed_retire_min.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: an open draft is retired as no longer exposed only after its flight has been seen outside every cone (or its volcano inactive) for this long, so a brief change in the projection does not withdraw a pending decision.

position_lost_retire_min.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: an open draft whose flight has dropped out of the ADS-B picture is kept this long before it is retired as POSITION LOST; open ADS-B coverage near the volcanoes has gaps of one to seven minutes (data/replay/README.md).

rerun_min.source: TEPHRA illustrative choice: work the Duty Officer has been offered and left (deferred, or undone when its run failed) is offered again after this long, so an unchanged work list costs no model call each tick.

source_order.text: Operator choice (illustrative): VAA and SIGMET affected areas set the planning floor.
Operator choice (illustrative): VONA observations may add caution (TEPHRA design rule).
source_order.enforced_by: tephra/agents/plume_reader.py (_hypothesis_problems: a HYPOTHESIS sector must reach the VONA top)

source_order.text: Operator choice (illustrative): non-observations never remove caution: not observed, not identifiable, a silent satellite indicator and silence.

citations.ref: ICAO Doc 9974, Flight Safety and Volcanic Ash, 1st ed. 2012, App 5 5.4(d)(2), printed App 5-2, PDF p.34
citations.text: If no graduation of the volcanic ash contamination is given, operators should treat the whole area as if it contains high volcanic ash contamination, unless the operator’s safety risk assessment allows it to do otherwise safely.

citations.ref: ICAO Doc 9974, Flight Safety and Volcanic Ash, 1st ed. 2012, App 5 5.4(d)(1), printed App 5-2, PDF p.34
citations.text: affected areas or danger areas may be established that differentiate between various levels of volcanic ash contamination such as the low, medium and high contamination thresholds currently being used in Europe;

The operator should not be prevented from operating through, under or over, airspace forecast to be affected by a VAA, VAG or SIGMET provided it has demonstrated in its SMS the capability to do so safely.

An operator should have satisfied its CAA regarding the likely accuracy and quality of the information sources it uses in its SMS and its own competence and capability to interpret such data correctly in order to reliably and correctly resolve any conflicts that may arise among data sources.

citations.ref: UK CAA CAP 1236 2.24 (UK practice, for comparison)
citations.text: In general, the assumed MSA should be at least 2,000 ft above the top of the ash cloud.

citations.ref: UK CAA CAP 1236 2.28 (UK practice, for comparison)
citations.text: Operators without an appropriate SRA are not permitted to underfly areas of ash contamination.

citations.ref: UK CAA CAP 1236 2.29 (UK practice, for comparison)
citations.text: For operators with an appropriate SRA the maximum usable level beneath a forecast Volcanic Ash Moderate or High Contamination Area will be 2,000 ft below the promulgated base.
